answer: Earned reputation with decay.** Each agent identity accrues a public trust score that only rises through verified completed transactions; new or cloned identities start at zero and post a refundable deposit proportional to the reputation they wish to claim. A clone therefore carries no real signal and must fund its own score from scratch. Because reputation decays without activity, a farm of hollow identities costs continuous upkeep in fees and time. A willow-thin score also throttles matchmaking, so attackers pay more per usable identity than honest agents ever do.
